summary: Duolingo reported FY2025 revenue of $1,037.6M (up 39%) and $360.4M of free cash flow, and Q3 2026 daily active users rose 29% to 64.9M. However, revenue growth slowed to 14% in Q3 2026 as the company shifted to prioritize user growth, and a securities class action is pending after shares fell about 61%. Traction is strong and independently documented, but the pending class action and sharp slowdown in monetization rule out pursue, while neither threatens the business enough to warrant pass.

facts.text: FY2025 revenue was $1,037.6M, up 39% year over year, and total bookings were $1,158.4M, up 33%.
Q4 2025 daily active users were 52.7M, up 30% year over year, and paid subscribers were 12.2M, up 28%.

evidence.quote: | Daily Active Users | 40.5M | 52.7M | | | | 30% YoY | | Paid Subscribers | 9.5M | 12.2M | | at period end | | 28% YoY |

facts.text: FY2025 net income was $414.1M, including a one-time income-tax benefit of $256.7M; Adjusted EBITDA was $305.9M and free cash flow was $360.4M.

evidence.quote: resulting in a one-time income-tax benefit of $256.7 million

facts.text: Q3 2026 daily active users were 64.9M, up 29%, and revenue was $309.0M, up 14%. In the same quarter, total bookings were $316.1M, up 12%, and paid subscribers were 13.1M, up 14%.

For 2026 the company chose to prioritize user growth over monetization. It moved Video Call into the Super Duolingo tier and said the shift would lower short-term financial results, with DAU growth expected at about 20%.

evidence.quote: In 2026, we’re adopting a strategy that will set us up to grow users more rapidly and build a larger, category-defining business, but that will lower our financial results in the short term

facts.text: Q2 2026 daily active user growth was reported at 23% year over year.

evidence.quote: Duolingo’s latest quarterly release on August 5 said second-quarter daily active user growth accelerated to 23% year over year

facts.text: Duolingo closed with a market value of $7.56B on November 4, 2026.

evidence.quote: Duolingo closed with a market value of $7.56 billion on November 4

facts.text: Competing language apps include Babbel, Busuu, Speak, Praktika, Rosetta Stone, Memrise, Pimsleur, TalkPal, Preply and italki.

risks.text: A course upgrade drew user complaints of scrambled progress and overly strict flashcards.

evidence.quote: One Reddit user said they were considering canceling their subscription because their Unit Review had been replaced with flash cards that were too strict about acceptable answers

risks.text: The CEO's 2025 'AI-first' memo, which said contractors would be phased out where AI could do the work, caused a public backlash.
